extracted.intended_audience: UK universities' research administrators, REF submission teams, and academics preparing REF 2021 submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Official panel criteria and working methods for REF 2021, specifying how Units of Assessment are evaluated across outputs, impact, and environment, the star-rating scale, submission requirements, and panel procedures. Intended to guide preparation and assessment of REF submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Outputs (component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Outputs — 60% of the overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs are individually assessed by sub-panel members using the universal criteria (originality, significance, rigour). Submission rule: average 2.5 outputs per FTE academic staff member (one per author minimum, five maximum for any individual). Output-level scores are aggregated using a 'quality profile' approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Impact (component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Impact — 25% of the overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact assessed via impact case studies; assessed against impact-specific criteria (reach and significance). Submission rule: minimum 2 case studies; rate of 1 per 15 FTE, plus 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Environment (component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Environment — 15% of the overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment assessed on vitality and sustainability, supported by an evidence base (research income, doctoral degrees awarded, research infrastructure) and an environment statement narrative describing strategies and institutional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Star Ratings (master scoring rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: All three components rated on a 5-point scale: 4★, 3★, 2★, 1★, Unclassified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 4★ — 'World-leading' quality in terms of originality, significance, and rigour; 3★ — 'Internationally excellent' in terms of originality, significance, and rigour, but falls short of the highest standards; 2★ — 'Recognised internationally' in terms of originality, significance, and rigour; 1★ — 'Recognised nationally' in terms of originality, significance, and rigour; Unclassified — falls below the standard of nationally recognised work, or does not meet the published definition of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (universal criterion for outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality — 'extent to which the output makes an important and innovative contribution to the field.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied at output level (and informs star-rating). Panels judge whether the work offers important and innovative contributions relative to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (universal criterion for outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance — 'extent to which the output has influenced, or has the capacity to influence, knowledge and scholarly thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed at output level for its influence on knowledge and scholarly debate; informs star-rating alongside originality and rigour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour (universal criterion for outputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigour — 'extent to which the output demonstrates intellectual coherence and integrity, and adopts robust and appropriate concepts, analyses, sources, theories, and methodologies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed at output level for methodological and intellectual soundness; a core component of the star-rating judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — Reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Reach — 'extent and diversity of beneficiaries' of the research impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess impact case studies; panels consider how many and what kinds of beneficiaries were affected by the research and the breadth/diversity of that influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact Significance — 'degree to which the impact has enabled, enriched, influenced, informed, or changed the performance, policies, practices, products, services, understanding, awareness, or well-being of the beneficiaries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed in impact case studies; focuses on the depth and importance of change caused by the research rather than academic influence alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment — Vitality
rubrics_metrics.description: Vitality — 'quality and scale of research activity, including PhD student support, research income, infrastructure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels judge how active and vibrant the research environment is, considering doctoral training, income attracted, facilities, and overall scale/quality of research activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment — Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustainability — 'strategies for maintaining and developing the research environment over time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers whether there are credible plans and institutional support to sustain and develop the research environment into the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment — Evidence base
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence base for Environment — use of research income, doctoral degrees awarded, research infrastructure, and an environment statement narrative as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment submissions must supply data (income, doctoral degrees, infrastructure) and a narrative environment statement to substantiate claims about vitality and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement — Outputs per FTE and individual limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs submission rules — '2.5 outputs per FTE academic staff member on average (one per author min, five max for any individual)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how many outputs each Unit of Assessment should submit on average, and limits per individual staff member to ensure fairness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement — Impact case studies count
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact case studies submission rules — 'minimum 2; rate of 1 per 15 FTE, plus 1.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the minimum and scaled number of impact case studies a unit must submit according to its staff FTE; influences the unit's ability to demonstrate impacts across its portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirement — Environment statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment statement requirement — narrative plus data on income, infrastructure, doctoral degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units must provide a narrative environment statement alongside quantitative data to allow panels to assess vitality and sustainability; this is a policy-driven submission component rather than an output or case study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel working methods and aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel structure and procedures — 4 Main Panels (A–D) and 34 Sub-Panels; sub-panel members read and grade outputs with cross-referencing; output-level scores aggregated using a 'quality profile' approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the procedural rubric for assessment: disciplinary allocation to panels/sub-panels, reading and grading practices, cross-referencing between panel members, and aggregation of individual output scores into unit-level quality profiles used for funding allocation.
